title: Perf bench scratch - latency/throughput runs (Samir Shah 2026-03-15)
content:
Objective:
- Quick sweep to capture latency and throughput characteristics for open-7b quantized variants on a single A100 dev node. Looking for p50/p95, seqs/s and tokens/s across baseline, batching, and kv-cache configurations. Note: this is a scratchpad, not final report.

Environment:
- Node: dev-a100-01 (1x A100 40GB)
- Runtime: serving-runtime v2.3.1-build45
- CUDA: 12.1, cuDNN: 9.0
- Model tested: open-7b-int8 (fp16 base converted to 8-bit quantized build)
- Sequence length used: input 512 tokens + generation 128 tokens = 640 tokens total (avg)
- Harness: perf/harness_v2.py (simple sync client; reports per-request latencies and aggregate throughput)

Commands used (local dev):
- Baseline (no cache, single):
  python perf/harness_v2.py --model open-7b-int8 --batch 1 --concurrency 1 --seq 640 --iter 200 --out run-baseline-2026-03-15.log

- Batching + concurrency (no kv-cache):
  python perf/harness_v2.py --model open-7b-int8 --batch 8 --concurrency 16 --seq 640 --iter 500 --out run-batch8-conc16-nocache.log

- Batching + concurrency + kv-cache enabled:
  python perf/harness_v2.py --model open-7b-int8 --batch 8 --concurrency 16 --kv-cache true --seq 640 --iter 500 --out run-batch8-conc16-kvcache.log

Raw aggregated results (quick summary):
Mode | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | seqs/s | tokens/s
Baseline | 120 | 240 | 8.3 | 5,312
Batch 8, conc 16, no-cache | 210 | 420 | 30 | 19,200
Batch 8, conc 16, kv-cache | 95 | 180 | 58 | 37,120

Notes on results and observations:
- Baseline: per-request latency low for single concurrency, but throughput limited (~8 seqs/s). p95 spikes come from occasional CUDA context setup on first few requests.
- Batching w/o cache: throughput increases (~19k tokens/s), but p95 degrades significantly due to head-of-line blocking in the batch when one request has a longer generation path. Seen queue build-up at concurrency >12.
- Kv-cache + batching: best overall from an app perspective when requests share prefixes. p50 and p95 improved compared to batching alone, and tokens/s nearly doubled vs batching alone. This indicates KV cache avoids recomputing large prefix attention and reduces time spent in forward passes.
- CPU/tokenization cost: measured ~15% CPU overhead across runs. Tokenization CPU becomes visible at higher concurrency and slightly limits seqs/s.
- Spikes: observed periodic 400-600ms spikes in all runs (more visible in no-cache case). Trace indicates Python GC pauses inside worker process during tokenizer initialization and logging flushes.

Quick hypotheses / actionable items:
- Default deploy strategy for chat routes: enable kv-cache by default, keep max_batch_size=8, target concurrency ~8-12 per GPU for stable p95.
- Investigate Python GC and logging flush behavior: reduce logging level in the hot path and pre-warm tokenizer objects. Possibly switch tokenization to a shared C-extension or run tokenization in a separate pool.
- Add tokenization microbenchmarks to perf/scripts to quantify CPU vs GPU split at multiple concurrencies.
- Run 24-hour stability test with mixed traffic: 30% repeat-prefix, 70% cold-start prompts to measure long-term p95 and memory growth (KV cache retention).

Next steps / todo:
- [ ] Create 24h load job (describe mix) and schedule on dev-A100 or dedicated cluster (JIRA-3421).
- [ ] Add GC and memory tracing to harness logs (small change in harness_v2).
- [ ] Run tokenization-only benchmark and add to perf dashboard.
- [ ] Re-run same tests on an A100 80GB node and on a T4-based node to compare memory/latency tradeoffs.

Run log snippets (timestamps):
- run-baseline-2026-03-15 09:12:01 UTC - p50 120ms p95 240ms seqs/s 8.3
- run-batch8-conc16-nocache 2026-03-15 10:05:10 UTC - p50 210ms p95 420ms seqs/s 30
- run-batch8-conc16-kvcache 2026-03-15 11:40:22 UTC - p50 95ms p95 180ms seqs/s 58

Notes-to-self:
- these are noisy short runs; use caution when extrapolating. Need longer runs and synthetic mix.
- share top-line numbers with Maya and Ethan for quick sync.

Attachments / links:
- full logs uploaded to perf-archive/run-baseline-2026-03-15.log (internal drive link pending)
- PR for tiny harness improvements: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1287

End of scratchpad.
